name: Soybean
sowing_window: November to December (first crop); December after a winter cereal (second crop).

rotation.notes: Repeating it increases late-season diseases and stink bugs; it shares pathogens with peanut.

kc_source: FAO-56 (Allen et al., 1998), Table 12: crop coefficients Kc
ky_source: FAO-33 (Doorenbos and Kassam, 1979): yield response factor to water Ky, full cycle
agronomic_notes: It fixes nitrogen, but exports a lot in the grain: the net N balance is close to zero. It leaves little residue that breaks down quickly, so the wind-erosion risk is high. The critical period is grain filling (R3-R6).
sources: FAO-56 (Allen et al., 1998), Table 12: crop coefficients Kc
FAO-33 (Doorenbos and Kassam, 1979): yield response factor to water Ky, full cycle

name: Corn
sowing_window: Early: September to October. Late: December (more common in rainfed fields, to avoid drought at flowering).

rotation.notes: Repeating it increases pests (fall armyworm, stem borer) and the corn leafhopper that spreads corn stunt.

kc_source: FAO-56 (Allen et al., 1998), Table 12: crop coefficients Kc
ky_source: FAO-33 (Doorenbos and Kassam, 1979): yield response factor to water Ky, full cycle
agronomic_notes: It uses the most water in the catalog and is very sensitive to drought at flowering. It leaves a lot of residue: it protects the soil and adds carbon. Its rainfed yield in San Luis depends heavily on water stored at planting.
sources: FAO-56 (Allen et al., 1998), Table 12: crop coefficients Kc
FAO-33 (Doorenbos and Kassam, 1979): yield response factor to water Ky, full cycle

name: Wheat
sowing_window: May to July.

rotation.notes: It shares diseases with barley; avoid wheat after wheat.

kc_source: FAO-56 (Allen et al., 1998), Table 12: crop coefficients Kc
ky_source: FAO-33 (Doorenbos and Kassam, 1979): yield response factor to water Ky, full cycle (winter wheat)
agronomic_notes: San Luis gets little rain in winter: rainfed wheat depends on water stored in the soil profile, so its relative yield is low. Sensitive to heat waves during grain filling. It allows second-crop soybean if water is left over.
sources: FAO-56 (Allen et al., 1998), Table 12: crop coefficients Kc

name: Sorghum
sowing_window: October to December, with warm soil.

rotation.notes: It shares pests with corn (aphids, stem borer).

kc_source: FAO-56 (Allen et al., 1998), Table 12: crop coefficients Kc (range 1.00-1.10; the midpoint is used)
ky_source: FAO-33 (Doorenbos and Kassam, 1979): yield response factor to water Ky, full cycle
agronomic_notes: More drought- and heat-tolerant than corn: it can pause growth and resume with rain. It leaves a lot of residue. Widely used for silage and grazing in mixed farms in San Luis.

name: Sunflower
sowing_window: September to December.

rotation.notes: Sclerotinia and Verticillium wilt mean it should not be repeated within 3 or 4 years; rapeseed shares Sclerotinia.

kc_source: FAO-56 (Allen et al., 1998), Table 12: crop coefficients Kc (range 1.00-1.15; the midpoint is used)
ky_source: FAO-33 (Doorenbos and Kassam, 1979): yield response factor to water Ky, full cycle
agronomic_notes: Deep roots: it uses water from deep layers and tolerates drought. It leaves little residue: high erosion risk. Birds cause damage.
sources: FAO-56 (Allen et al., 1998), Table 12: crop coefficients Kc

name: Peanut
sowing_window: October to November; includes lifting and drying in the field.

rotation.notes: Peanut smut requires long rotations; it shares pathogens with soybean.

kc_source: FAO-56 (Allen et al., 1998), Table 12: crop coefficients Kc
ky_source: FAO-33 (Doorenbos and Kassam, 1979): yield response factor to water Ky, full cycle
agronomic_notes: It suits the sandy soils of eastern San Luis. Lifting leaves the soil very loose and bare: it is the crop with the highest wind-erosion risk. It is usually sold under contract to processing plants.

name: Alfalfa
sowing_window: Autumn (March-April) or spring (September).

rotation.notes: Autotoxicity: do not reseed alfalfa after alfalfa without several years in between.

kc_source: FAO-56 (Allen et al., 1998), Table 12: crop coefficients Kc (average value including cutting effect)
ky_source: FAO-33 (Doorenbos and Kassam, 1979): yield response factor to water Ky, full cycle
agronomic_notes: Very deep roots: it uses water from layers other crops cannot reach, but it uses a lot over the year. It fixes nitrogen and improves soil structure. The basis of mixed crop-livestock systems.
sources: FAO-56 (Allen et al., 1998), Table 12: crop coefficients Kc

name: Perennial pasture
scientific_name: Mezcla según zona: p. ej. Eragrostis curvula, Digitaria eriantha, Medicago sativa
sowing_window: Autumn for mixes with alfalfa; spring-summer for warm-season grasses (weeping lovegrass, digitaria).

rotation.notes: When the pasture is broken up, a summer cereal is best to use the released nitrogen.

kc_source: FAO-56 (Allen et al., 1998), Table 12: crop coefficients Kc (pasture under rotational grazing, range 0.85-1.05)
ky_source: Assumption: the species is not listed in FAO-33; it is treated like a similar crop (perennial forage)

sowing_window: March to May; terminated in August-September.
